title: Real science: a solar storm hit Mars
text: On May 20, 2024, a huge solar flare was followed by fast charged particles that reached Mars within tens of minutes. A radiation detector on NASA's Curiosity rover measured about 8,100 micrograys at the surface. NASA compared that to 30 chest X-rays. It was not deadly, but it was the biggest jump that detector had seen since landing. Thick rock, like cliffs or lava tubes, could give astronauts extra shielding.
gameNote: Game rule: this storm gives a 30-point radiation burst. Points are game units, not real units.

title: Why dust matters for power
text: Solar panels make power from sunlight. When dust fills the air, less light reaches them, so there is less power to share between your systems.
gameNote: Game rule: this storm blocks 60% of sunlight for 5 days. The numbers are invented, and real data on dust storms is not used yet.
